questions.question: Which of these is a primitive type in Java?
questions.explanation: int is a primitive type; Integer is its wrapper class, and String and ArrayList are classes.

questions.question: Which keyword creates a new object from a class?
questions.explanation: new allocates an object and calls its constructor, e.g. new Student().

questions.question: Which collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set such as HashSet stores each element at most once; lists allow duplicates.

questions.question: Which SQL statement reads rows from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT ... FROM table returns rows; the other keywords are not SQL statements.

questions.question: Which clause filters groups after GROUP BY?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY.

questions.question: What does a LEFT JOIN return?
options: Only rows that match in both tables
All rows from the left table, plus matching rows from the right table
All rows from the right table only
Every combination of rows from both tables
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps every left row and fills right-side columns with NULL when there is no match.

questions.question: In Spring, what is dependency injection?
options: Injecting SQL into a query string
Adding JAR files to the classpath
The framework supplies an object's dependencies instead of the object creating them
Loading every class at startup with reflection
questions.explanation: Spring creates beans and passes them in (usually through the constructor), so classes don't build their own dependencies.

questions.question: Which annotation marks a class whose methods handle REST requests and return response bodies?
questions.explanation: @RestController combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, so return values become the HTTP response body.

questions.question: In Spring Data JPA, what do you usually write to get CRUD methods for an entity?
options: A class that implements every SQL query by hand
An XML mapping file per table
questions.explanation: Declaring interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> gives save, findById, findAll, delete and more.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code means "Not Found"?
questions.explanation: 404 means the resource doesn't exist; 200 is OK, 301 is a redirect and 500 is a server error.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is normally used to create a new resource in a REST API?
questions.explanation: POST /students creates a student; GET, HEAD and OPTIONS only read.

questions.question: Which of these is valid JSON?
questions.explanation: JSON keys and strings must use double quotes; the last option is XML.

questions.question: In JUnit 5, which annotation marks a test method?
questions.explanation: Methods annotated with @Test (org.junit.jupiter.api.Test) are run as tests.

questions.question: What is a mock object used for in a unit test?
options: To replace a real dependency with a controllable fake
questions.explanation: A mock stands in for a dependency (like a repository) so the class under test can be checked in isolation.

questions.question: Which tool lets you test Spring MVC controllers without starting a real server?
questions.explanation: MockMvc sends simulated HTTP requests to controllers inside the test.

questions.question: Which command records staged changes in the repository history?
questions.explanation: git add stages changes, git commit records them, git push uploads commits to a remote.

questions.question: You are on main and run `git merge feature`. What happens?
options: main is uploaded to the remote
The changes from feature are combined into main
questions.explanation: git merge brings the other branch's commits into the current branch.

questions.question: In a Maven project, where are dependencies declared?
questions.explanation: Maven reads dependencies from the <dependencies> section of pom.xml.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of reading an array element by its index?
questions.explanation: The address of a[i] is computed directly, so access takes constant time.

questions.question: Two nested loops each run n times. How does the total work grow?
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs n times for each of the n outer iterations: n × n = n².

questions.question: The recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n), as in merge sort, solves to:
questions.explanation: There are log n levels of halving and each level does O(n) work in total.

questions.question: How long does inserting a new node at the head of a singly linked list take?
questions.explanation: Point the new node at the old head and update the head pointer: constant work.

questions.question: Which data structure works Last-In, First-Out (LIFO)?
questions.explanation: A stack pops the most recently pushed element first; a queue is First-In, First-Out.

questions.question: What is the average-case time to look up a key in a hash table?
questions.explanation: Hashing jumps straight to a bucket; with a good hash function buckets stay small.

questions.question: What must be true of the data for binary search to work?
options: It is stored in a linked list
questions.explanation: Binary search discards half the range each step, which is only valid when the data is sorted.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort always splits evenly, so even the worst case is O(n log n) (unlike quicksort's O(n²)).

questions.question: What happens when a recursive function has no base case?
options: The compiler adds a base case automatically
It keeps calling itself until the call stack overflows
questions.explanation: Without a base case nothing stops the recursion, so it ends in a StackOverflowError.

questions.question: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order visits left subtree, node, right subtree, which follows the BST ordering.

questions.question: In a min-heap, where is the smallest element?
questions.explanation: Every parent is ≤ its children, so the minimum is always at the root.

questions.question: Level-order (breadth-first) traversal of a tree uses which helper structure?
questions.explanation: A queue processes nodes in the order they were discovered, one level at a time.

questions.question: Which algorithm finds the path with the fewest edges in an unweighted graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores vertices in order of distance (edge count) from the start.

questions.question: Dijkstra's algorithm can give wrong answers on graphs with:
questions.explanation: Dijkstra assumes a settled distance never improves, which negative edges can break (use Bellman-Ford instead).

questions.question: A topological ordering of the vertices exists only for:
questions.explanation: A cycle would need a vertex to come before itself, so only DAGs can be topologically sorted.

questions.question: How does memoization speed up a recursive solution?
options: It stores the result of each subproblem so it is computed only once
It runs the recursive calls in parallel
questions.explanation: Overlapping subproblems are looked up instead of recomputed, e.g. Fibonacci drops from O(2ⁿ) to O(n).

questions.question: What does a greedy algorithm do?
options: Makes the locally best choice at each step
questions.explanation: Greedy commits to the best-looking choice now; it is optimal only for some problems.

questions.question: Computing the n-th Fibonacci number with bottom-up dynamic programming takes:
questions.explanation: Each value from 2 to n is computed once from the previous two.
